title: berths-carry-request-identity
intention: The berth handoff carries request identity: a resolver verb answers 'the deepest berth claiming ticket X' as a command, and every chart gate refuses a *_ref berth whose ticket claim disagrees with the packet claiming it — the silent wrong-chain voyage becomes a loud refusal.
why: Rank 1 of notes/2026-08-02-opus-compatibility-pass.json, ruled spec by 2026-08-03-projections-stand — the pass's ONE silent-corruption path: after a compact, a session opens a flat packets directory with dozens of berths from many requests and must eyeball the right one; /sail step 0 says 'deepest link first' and gives no command. Pick a stale berth and the whole voyage sails green under another request's chain — every door passes, wrong build, nothing ever says so. The deterministic lookup already half-exists (latest_claiming_artifact, cairn/machines/chart/verdict.py) and no skill mentions it; the chain links already exist and assert integrity but not identity.
traces_to: Law 4 — nine conversation-carried handoffs become physics in one stroke

proves_green.proof_gate: proof teeth beside the code (cairn/machines/chart/proofs/), bare twice, sealed under the tester (netns), validations beside the code
proves_green.entry_gate: BUILDME rides the chart chain + intent berth + sorted berth
proves_green.durability_gate: not done until proven AND committed (git)

falsifier.proves_red: RED if: a packet claiming ticket A passes a gate while its ref'd berth claims ticket B; or the resolver returns a shallower berth when a deeper one claims the ticket; or a claimless chain is newly refused (jurisdiction creep — identity is checked only where BOTH sides claim).
falsifier.horizon: the next post-compact session recovers its chain by the resolver command instead of eyeballing the packets directory — that recovery is the lived measure
